doc.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Introduction and Polcer's passion for perpetuating jazz
summary: Monk Rowe introduces Polcer; Polcer says he enjoys promoting and band leading as much as playing.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe. We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Tarrytown, and I’m quite pleased to have Ed Polcer, cornetist and one man vanguard to keep jazz and swing alive in this country.
I shouldn’t say one man I suppose, because there’s other people out there.
Many doing it. But it seems to be quite a passion of yours.

Yes. I’ve always had that passion to go beyond just the playing. I don’t like the word preservation but the perpetuation of this great music, and I think I enjoy the promoting of it and the band leading as much as I do the playing.
